title: Shallow Structs (Getter/Setter Classitis)
pattern: A struct containing private data wrapped entirely in simple getter and setter methods with absolutely no internal invariants, data validation, or core business logic.
why_bad: Creates a shallow abstraction. The cost of learning and writing calls to the interface (getters/setters) is equal to or greater than interacting with the fields directly. It provides a false sense of encapsulation while leaking the exact shape of the private data to consumers, leading to high interface maintenance.
detection: Structs where 100% of fields are accessed or modified via 1-to-1 matching public getters/setters with no guard conditions, calculations, or invariant verification.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Shared libraries exporting stable binary interfaces (ABIs) where direct field exposure could break backwards compatibility.
source: *John K. Ousterhout - A Philosophy of Software Design (2018)*, Chapter 4, "Modules Should Be Deep" (Shallow Modules, p. 25 & Classitis, p. 26).
